about.note: The cross-validated Auto MPG study at the end (lot P).

plan.title: Discover the data
plan.question: What does one row describe, which columns are there and what does each one mean, and what do a few rows look like?
plan.expected_output: The data card read with you: the row unit, the columns grouped with their meaning and availability, and a few example rows. Nothing is decided at this step.
plan.completion: Done once a first proposal is made.

plan.title: Define the prediction moment
plan.question: At what moment is the prediction made, and what is known at that moment?
plan.expected_output: A confirmed prediction time, restated and answered in your own words.

plan.title: Decide which variables are available at prediction time
plan.question: Which variables are known at the prediction moment, and which must be excluded?
plan.expected_output: A confirmed availability status for every candidate feature, with the exclusions listed in your own words.

plan.title: Split the data before exploring it
plan.question: How is the development set divided into folds for k-fold cross-validation, before any exploration of the target? Each fold is in turn the validation fold, predicted by a model fitted on the other folds, the training folds.
plan.expected_output: A confirmed cross-validation and a recorded fold assignment.
plan.completion: Decision split is confirmed and the split result is current.

plan.title: Choose how the error is measured
plan.question: The error of one prediction is the gap between the observed value and the predicted one. The mean absolute error (MAE) averages these gaps; the root mean squared error (RMSE) averages their squares, then takes the root, so one big miss weighs much more. Which of the two measures the error of this study? It is chosen now, before any model is fitted.
plan.expected_output: A confirmed error measure (MAE or RMSE), chosen before any model result is seen.

plan.title: Fix the success criterion before seeing a model
plan.question: The mean absolute error is the average size of a prediction's error, in the unit of the target. The mean baseline predicts, for every row of a validation fold, the mean of the training folds. How much smaller than the error of the mean baseline should the out-of-fold error of the model be for it to be worth using? It is fixed now, before any model is fitted.
plan.expected_output: A confirmed minimum relative error reduction over the mean baseline, stated before any model result is seen.

plan.title: Check the structure of the data
plan.question: Which columns have missing cells, rare categories, or values outside their possible range? This check reads the development rows without the target, so the preparation decided from it comes before any look at the target.
plan.expected_output: A current quality overview of the development rows, read without the target.

plan.title: Decide how the model prepares the variables
plan.question: How should the model treat missing values, rare categories, extreme values and skewed variables? The draft reads the quality check, which does not read the target; every parameter is learnt only on the rows each model is fitted on.
plan.expected_output: A confirmed preprocessing, with the explorations that motivated it.

plan.title: Explore the target on the development rows
plan.question: What do the development rows show about the distribution of the target and the special values? Each of these analyses is a look at the target: it reads the variable to predict, and every look is counted. The preparation is already decided, before these looks.
plan.expected_output: A target summary and special-value counts on the development rows, with their exposure recorded.
plan.completion: The training EDA results are current.

plan.title: Fit a mean baseline and a linear model
plan.question: Which predictions do the mean baseline and a linear model give for each development row, predicted out of fold?
plan.expected_output: Persisted out-of-fold predictions for the mean baseline and the linear model.

plan.title: Choose the variants to compare
plan.question: Which variants of the candidate model, at most three and each with the question it answers, should be compared with it under the same evaluation: the penalty chosen by nested cross-validation, a stronger or weaker regularisation, the model without one group of variables, or another model family when the diagnostics show a pattern the linear model cannot follow?
plan.expected_output: A confirmed list of variants and their out-of-fold predictions, evaluated like the candidate.
plan.completion: Decision model_variant is confirmed and every variant fit is current.

plan.title: Choose the model
plan.question: Does the linear model reduce the out-of-fold error of the mean baseline, in the target unit, by enough to adopt it, given the paired intervals and the residuals?
plan.expected_output: A current regression evaluation and a confirmed model choice.
plan.completion: The regression evaluation is current and decision model_choice is confirmed.

plan.title: Open the final test once
plan.question: Now that the model is chosen, do you open the sealed final test, once, to measure it on rows nothing has seen? After this, any change is made after the final test.
plan.expected_output: A confirmed opening in your own words, and the one evaluation of the chosen configuration on the final test.
plan.completion: Decision final_test is confirmed and the final evaluation is recorded.

plan.title: Conclude proportionately
plan.question: What can be said, for which use, and with which limits? Keeping the baseline is a valid result.
plan.expected_output: A confirmed conclusion that names its limits.

next_action.message: Every step is done. Review what is not yet defensible.
next_action.junior_message: Every step of the plan is done. Before relying on the conclusion, read the limits the report lists.
next_action.junior_digest: Every step of the plan is done. Before relying on the conclusion, read the limits the report lists. The success criterion is met on the holdout (final test).
next_action.plan_recap: The plan, in order: Frame the change (Data, Prediction moment, Available variables, Split, Error measure, Success criterion); Prepare evidence (Quality check, Preparation, Exploration); Work and compare (Models, Variants, Model choice); Conclude and hand over (Final test, Conclusion). Every step of the plan is done.

after_study.junior_text: What comes next: the handoff pack collects your decisions, the cited results and the limits for a reviewer. The chosen model, the linear regression, can also be exported as an Azure ML project: the export plan lists the files first and writes nothing. No Azure job or endpoint has ever been run from these exports: they are checked on this computer only.

limitations.text: Out-of-fold predictions on the development rows are used to compare the models and the variant, so they are development evidence, not independent evidence of future performance. Only the sealed final test, opened once, is.

eda_looks.note: Each exploration that read the target on training rows is a look, and so is each diagnostic of the models on the development rows. The count is a disclosure: the more looks, the more a pattern found among them can be chance. Validation and final-test rows are never explored.

trials.note: Each candidate or variant configuration fitted is a trial. Choosing the best of several trials on the same rows makes its figures slightly optimistic; the final test, opened once, is not affected.

configurations.question: Does a ridge penalty chosen by nested cross-validation predict with a smaller error than the unpenalised linear model?

difference.definition: per-fold paired difference (this configuration minus the candidate), mean plus or minus one standard error

configurations.question: Does an explainable boosting machine follow the curve of horsepower and weight?

difference.definition: per-fold paired difference (this configuration minus the candidate), mean plus or minus one standard error

one_se.source: Hastie, Tibshirani & Friedman (2009), The Elements of Statistical Learning, 2nd ed., §7.10 (the one-standard-error rule)
one_se.text: The one-standard-error rule keeps the simplest configuration whose mean is within one standard error of the best one.

texts.en: The one-standard-error rule keeps the simplest configuration whose mean is within one standard error of the best one.
texts.fr: La règle d'une erreur type retient la configuration la plus simple dont la moyenne est à moins d'une erreur type de la meilleure.

one_se.simplicity: the linear family first, then fewer features, then a stronger penalty; a tie keeps the candidate

optimism.method: mean over folds of (the fold's best configuration minus the configuration best on the mean), in the direction of the metric
optimism.source: Tibshirani & Tibshirani (2009), A bias correction for the minimum error rate in cross-validation, Annals of Applied Statistics 3(2): 822-829
optimism.text: Choosing the best of several configurations on the same folds flatters it: the optimism is the average gap, fold by fold, between that fold's best configuration and the one chosen.

texts.en: Choosing the best of several configurations on the same folds flatters it: the optimism is the average gap, fold by fold, between that fold's best configuration and the one chosen.
texts.fr: Choisir la meilleure de plusieurs configurations sur les mêmes plis la flatte : l'optimisme est l'écart moyen, pli par pli, entre la meilleure configuration du pli et celle retenue.

optimism.note: Approximate: an estimate of how much the best mean owes to having chosen it among these configurations.

advice.text: At least one variant differs from the candidate by more than the noise between folds. Another variant is possible within the budget, each one counted.

texts.en: At least one variant differs from the candidate by more than the noise between folds. Another variant is possible within the budget, each one counted.
texts.fr: Au moins une variante diffère du candidat de plus que le bruit entre les plis. Une autre variante reste possible dans le budget, chacune comptée.

model_selection.note: Development evidence: every configuration is compared on the same out-of-fold predictions of the development rows. The fold standard errors ignore the overlap of the folds' training rows (Bengio & Grandvalet 2004), so they understate the noise: the advice errs towards stopping late, not early. The final test, opened once, is not affected by this choice.

calibration_slope.definition: least-squares slope of the target on the prediction: 1 when the predictions are as spread as the target

checks.method: binned out-of-fold gaps per numeric feature (chi-square, Bonferroni); calibration slope by segment (Cochran's Q); overall calibration slope (Cox 1958)
checks.note: Checks of the candidate linear model on its out-of-fold predictions: a flag is evidence that another model family might follow the data more closely, not proof; choosing a family after seeing it makes that comparison data-contingent.

families.diagnostics: a shape function per feature and the pairwise interaction terms

families.diagnostics: permutation importance on the out-of-fold rows

model_families.text: The diagnostics of the linear model show a pattern it cannot follow; a non-linear family may be compared as one variant (a trial, chosen after seeing the diagnostics).
